topic: Korean convenience stores (pyeonuijeom): 53,266 stores of the big four at end-2025 (MOTIE via Asia Economy/fnnews), first-ever yearly drop since 1988; cook ramyeon inside, half-price parcels, safe household medicines since 2012-11-15, 1+1 deals, ATM and transit top-up, tourists' last stop
title: In Korea, the Convenience Store Does Almost Everything

slides.headline: In Korea, the convenience store **does almost everything.**
slides.note: Noodles, parcels and medicine at 3 a.m.

slides.headline: Cook **your noodles inside**
slides.body: Pick a cup of ramyeon (라면), add hot water at the machine and eat at the window counter. Near Seoul's Han River, some stores have machines that boil instant noodles for you.

slides.headline: Ship a parcel **for half price**
slides.body: Drop a box at one store and the buyer picks it up at another, often for about ₩2,000. People use it to send things they sell second-hand.

slides.headline: Medicine **after midnight**
slides.body: Since November 2012, stores can sell a short list of medicines: fever and pain pills, cold medicine, digestive aids and pain patches. Pharmacies close. The store doesn't.

slides.headline: Buy one, **get one free**
slides.body: Stickers that say 1+1 and 2+1 cover the drinks fridge and the snack aisle. The deals change every month, so regulars check before they pay.

slides.headline: Cash, **and your bus fare**
slides.body: Most stores have an ATM, and the counter tops up your transit card. Some hand out pre-ordered parcels and print photos too.

slides.headline: Tourists' **last stop**
slides.body: Visitors fill bags with snacks and ramyeon before flying home. GS25 said foreign shoppers spent 74.2% more there last year, and one Seoul store built a whole wall of noodles for them.

slides.headline: Stores of the **four biggest chains**
slides.body: Counted at the end of 2025, about one for every 960 people. It was also the first year the number went down since the first store opened in 1988.

slides.headline: Dinner **in a lunch box**
slides.body: Rice balls, kimbap and full lunch boxes called dosirak (도시락) fill the shelves. For students and people who live alone, the store is the kitchen.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: A Seoul convenience store glowing on a dark street, blurred behind the text.

caption:
Hot noodles at the window, a parcel at the counter, cold medicine at 2 a.m. In Korea, the convenience store on the corner handles all of it.

There are more than 53,000 of them.

What would you buy first in a Korean convenience store?
reply: Small tip: after you buy a cup of noodles or a lunch box, the hot-water machine and the microwave are free to use.
fact_check: 2장: 매장 온수기·취식대, 한강 편의점 즉석 라면 조리기(BGF리테일, 위키트리).
7장: GS25 외국인 결제금액 전년 대비 74.2% 증가, CU 홍대 '라면 도서관' 외국인 비중 70~75%(아시아경제 2026-06·위키트리).
reply: 구매 후 온수기·전자레인지 사용(업계 일반).
